gross_margin.label: Gross Margin
gross_margin.desc: Share of revenue left after the direct cost of delivery.
gross_margin.interpret: Higher is better; typical levels vary widely by industry, so set a target that fits yours.

operating_margin.label: Operating Margin
operating_margin.desc: Profitability from core operations, before interest and non-operating items.
operating_margin.interpret: Higher is better; compare it with the target you set.

ebitda_margin.label: EBITDA Margin
ebitda_margin.desc: Operating profitability before non-cash charges and financing.
ebitda_margin.interpret: Useful for comparing businesses with different capital structures; compare it with the target you set.

net_margin.label: Net Profit Margin
net_margin.desc: Bottom-line profit as a share of revenue, after everything.
net_margin.interpret: Higher is better; compare it with the target you set.

roa.label: Return on Assets
roa.desc: How efficiently the asset base generates profit, annualized for part-year periods.
roa.interpret: Higher is better; compare it with the target you set.

roe.label: Return on Equity
roe.desc: Return generated on shareholders' equity, annualized for part-year periods. Not meaningful when equity is negative.
roe.interpret: Higher is better; compare it with the target you set.

roic.label: Return on Invested Capital
roic.desc: Return on all capital invested. NOPAT = operating income × (1 − tax rate), using the effective rate booked for the period or else the statutory rate from tax setup. Invested capital = equity + the interest-bearing debt you classify.
roic.interpret: Above your cost of capital creates value; compare it with the target you set.

roce.label: Return on Capital Employed
roce.desc: Pre-tax operating return on the long-term capital employed in the business, annualized for part-year periods.
roce.interpret: Higher is better; compare it with the target you set.

rev_per_employee.label: Revenue per Employee
rev_per_employee.interpret: Benchmarks vary by industry, geography and currency; it is graded only against a target you set.

gp_per_employee.label: Gross Profit per Employee
gp_per_employee.desc: Value each employee contributes after direct costs.
gp_per_employee.interpret: A cleaner productivity signal than revenue per head.

asset_turnover.label: Asset Turnover
asset_turnover.desc: Revenue generated per unit of assets, annualized for part-year periods.
asset_turnover.interpret: Above 1.0× means assets turn over more than once a year.

cogs_ratio.label: COGS Ratio
cogs_ratio.desc: Direct cost of delivery as a share of revenue. Lower is better.
cogs_ratio.interpret: The inverse of gross margin — keep it below your target.

opex_ratio.label: OpEx Ratio
opex_ratio.desc: Overhead as a share of revenue. Lower is better.
opex_ratio.interpret: Controlling this is the lever between gross and operating margin.

operating_leverage.label: Operating Leverage
operating_leverage.desc: How much operating income moves for a given revenue change.
operating_leverage.interpret: Above 1.0x means profits scale faster than revenue.

interest_coverage.label: Interest Coverage
interest_coverage.desc: How many times operating income covers the interest expense on the accounts you classify as interest.
interest_coverage.interpret: Higher is safer; compare it with the target you set and your lenders' covenants.

rule_of_40.label: Rule of 40
rule_of_40.desc: Balances growth against profitability in a single number.
rule_of_40.interpret: Trade growth for margin or vice versa; compare it with the target you set.

current_ratio.label: Current Ratio
current_ratio.desc: Short-term assets available for each unit of obligations due within a year.
current_ratio.interpret: Below 1.0× means current obligations exceed current assets.

quick_ratio.label: Quick Ratio
quick_ratio.desc: Obligations due within a year covered by cash and receivables alone, without selling inventory.
quick_ratio.interpret: At or above 1.0× means near-term obligations are covered without inventory.

working_capital.label: Working Capital
working_capital.desc: The short-term resources left after meeting obligations due within a year.
working_capital.interpret: Negative working capital means current obligations exceed current assets.

debt_to_equity.label: Debt to Equity
debt_to_equity.desc: Financial leverage: borrowed money per unit of owners' equity, using the debt accounts you classify. Lower is safer.
debt_to_equity.interpret: Lower is safer; compare it with the target you set and your lenders' covenants.

liabilities_to_equity.label: Liabilities to Equity
liabilities_to_equity.desc: Everything the business owes per unit of owners' equity. Lower is safer.
liabilities_to_equity.interpret: Lower is safer; compare it with the target you set.

grading.title: How grades are computed
grading.body: Each ratio is compared with its target. Achieving {a} of the target or more earns an A, {b} a B, {c} a C and {d} a D; below that is an F. For lower-is-better ratios (costs, leverage) the comparison is inverted. A ratio without a target, or without the data it needs, is shown but not graded.
grading.labels: The health score averages the graded categories: {excellent}+ reads Excellent, {good}+ Good, {average}+ Average, and below that Needs Work. Every one of these values is set in Thresholds.

analysis.rsfNote: = amount ÷ the vendor's historical 2nd-largest transaction in the same currency ({months}-month baseline, computed in one window-function pass). RSF ≥ {threshold} means a transaction wildly out of scale for that vendor — a classic error/fraud signal.
analysis.zscoreNote: measures how many standard deviations a transaction sits from that vendor's own average in the same currency (per-vendor, per-currency baselines over {months} months, one aggregate pass). |z| ≥ {threshold} flags entity-specific outliers that global thresholds miss.

duplicates.ruleNote: same vendor + kind + currency + amount + reference, ≥{min}

sequential.indicatorNote1: if a vendor's invoice numbers to you are perfectly sequential over weeks or months, you are likely their
sequential.indicatorNote2: customer. Legitimate vendors have numbering gaps from invoicing others. Detected by scanning every vendor's reference numbers per currency for unbroken runs.

ghost.title: Ghost vendors
ghost.note: Two-phase matching across the full party registry: employee names against vendor names (role-verified employees only), and street addresses shared between a paid vendor and an employee (line 1 + postal code + country, script-preserving normalization). Point values are listed under Configuration → Scoring model.

sentinel.auditNote: Native audit log. Most records in this ledger were bulk-migrated, so change history begins at go-live — the trail grows as users work in openbooks.
sentinel.trapNote: Amounts just below a real approval limit (ending in 99, 999, or 9999) can indicate purchases engineered to stay under that limit. Limits come from the approval Flows; with no amount condition in Flows this check reports unavailable instead of risk. Traps always read the document amount in its own currency.
